candidate.answerReason: Under the recorded independent, uniform spinner model, there are nine equally likely ordered pairs. Exactly five have an even sum.

methods.label: Enumerate the spinner outcomes
methods.explanation: Listing the outcomes in a table gives 9 equally likely outcomes. The 5 outcomes with an even sum are \((1,1)\), \((1,3)\), \((2,2)\), \((3,1)\), and \((3,3)\). The probability that Player A wins is \(5/9\), which is greater than \(1/2\), so the game is unfair.
methods.levelReason: Outcome tables and equally likely probabilities are within Grade 9; the additional fairness comparison uses elementary fractions.

methods.label: Group outcomes by parity
methods.explanation:
With independent spins and equally likely sections, all ordered pairs of labels are equally likely. An even sum occurs exactly when both labels are odd or both are even. Each spinner has two odd labels, 1 and 3, and one even label, 2. Thus there are \(2\cdot2=4\) odd-odd pairs and \(1\cdot1=1\) even-even pair. These cases are disjoint and cover every even sum. Out of the \(3\cdot3=9\) possible pairs, Player A therefore wins with probability
\[
\frac{2\cdot2+1\cdot1}{3\cdot3}=\frac59.
\]
methods.levelReason: Parity grouping and elementary pairing counts give a different organizing idea without requiring high-school probability rules.

candidate.annotationRationale:

The retained method uses outcome tabulation; its extra fairness conclusion uses cnm_289 but is not an additional assessed demand. The alternative uses parity classes and simple pairing counts. Parity recognition and the equally likely model support both methods.
